06-1.author: Johannes Hevelius, from his book Machina coelestis (first part), published in 1673.
06-1.caption: Hevelius's giant open-frame telescope hangs from a tall mast by ropes as a crowd watches near Danzig (1673).

06-2.author: Christiaan Huygens
06-2.caption: Huygens's tubeless 'aerial telescope' (1684): the lens sits high on a pole, the observer stands on the ground.

06-3.author: Christiaan Huygens
06-3.caption: Page from Huygens's Systema Saturnium (1659) showing how Saturn's rings look different as it circles the Sun.

07-1.author: User:Solipsist (Andrew Dunn)
07-1.caption: Replica of Isaac Newton's small reflecting telescope of 1672, with its eyepiece on the side of the tube.

07-2.author: Szőcs Tamás Tamasflex
07-2.caption: Inside a Newtonian telescope: the curved main mirror sends light to a small flat mirror, then out to the eyepiece.

07-3.author: Isaac Newton
07-3.caption: Newton's own sketch of his two-prism experiment, from his 1672 letter to the Royal Society about light and colour.

08-1.file: Joseph von Fraunhofer, engraving by Christian Gottlob Scherff.jpg
08-1.author: Christian Gottlob Scherff, b. ca.1793 (engraver)
08-1.caption: Engraved portrait of Joseph von Fraunhofer, the German glassmaker and optician who made superb telescope lenses.

08-2.author: Joseph Fraunhofer
08-2.caption: Fraunhofer's own hand-coloured etching of the Sun's spectrum, with its dark lines labelled A to I.

08-3.author: Elen Torb
08-3.caption: Fraunhofer's great refractor, built for Dorpat (now Tartu) Observatory in Estonia, on display in the old observatory.

09-1.author: Lemuel Francis Abbott
09-1.caption: William Herschel, painted by Lemuel Francis Abbott in 1785, a few years after he discovered Uranus.

09-2.file: 40 foot telescope 120 cm 48 inch reflecting telescope William Herschel.png
09-2.author: Andrew Bell and Colin Macfarquhar
09-2.caption: Engraving of Herschel's giant 40-foot telescope in its wooden frame of ladders, from the 1797 Encyclopaedia Britannica.

09-3.author: M. F. Tielemanm
09-3.caption: Caroline Herschel, astronomer and comet hunter, in a portrait painted in 1829.

10-1.file: George Washington's field telescope, used during the Revolutionary War - National Museum of American History - DSC00167.jpg
10-1.author: Daderot
10-1.caption: George Washington's brass and wood draw-tube field telescope and leather case, at the National Museum of American History.

10-2.file: London Royal Observatory with the time ball - panoramio.jpg
10-2.author: Nikolai Karaneschev
10-2.caption: Flamsteed House at the Royal Observatory, Greenwich, with the red time ball that drops at 1 pm every day.

10-3.author: Tamasflex
10-3.caption: Cutaway of Porro prism binoculars: light passes the big lens, zigzags through two prisms, then reaches the eyepiece.
